positive.prompt: Write a one-off script to delete duplicate invoices for one customer in production
Review this UPDATE before ops runs it against the live database
Backfill the new status column for existing rows in batches without locking the table
How should we name, version, and document our SQL data fix scripts?

negative.prompt: Make our seed script idempotent so it can run on every deploy
Profile the slow orders page and add the missing index

evals.expected_output: A new reviewed-ready SQL script named per the folder convention, with a header, a tenant-scoped preview of the duplicates, a backup of the rows to delete, handling of payments that reference duplicates, a transaction with a row-count guard, and a written rollback, without executing anything
expectations: A new file in db/scripts is named with the date, OPS-214, and a short description, following the README convention, and starts with a header giving purpose, ticket, tenant scope, how to run it, and how to roll back
Every statement that reads or changes invoices filters on organization_id = 42
The script previews the duplicate rows and their count with the same predicate used by the delete, keeping the earliest-created row per invoice number (by created_at, with id as a tiebreaker)
Rows to be deleted are copied to a backup table or export before deletion, and payments that reference a duplicate are repointed to the kept invoice or the script stops, rather than being ignored
The delete runs inside a transaction and aborts or rolls back if the affected row count differs from the previewed count
The agent does not execute the script against any database, and states the expected row count must be confirmed from the preview before applying
